description: Soybean mosaic virus (SMV) is a widespread plant virus affecting primarily soybean, causing leaf mosaic, stunting, reduced pod number, and seed discoloration. Yield loss and reduced seed quality can occur.
distribution: Worldwide in all soybean-growing areas, particularly in temperate and subtropical regions.

host_range.general: Mostly Glycine max (cultivated soybean) and G. soja (wild soybean)

leaf: Mottling with light and dark green patches

damage: Reduced seed quality, size, and germination
Symptoms may be mild or absent in high temperatures
Severe impact when co-infected with other viruses (e.g., BPMV)

biology.particle: Filamentous particles ~7500 Å long, 120 Å diameter
biology.genome: Single-stranded positive-sense RNA (~9.6 kb) with VPg protein at 5′ end, encoding a single polyprotein processed into ~10 functional proteins
biology.favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures (16–28°C), aphid activity promotes spread
biology.seed_transmission_rate: Typically <5%, but variable depending on cultivar

cultural_control: Plant early in the season to reduce impact
genetic_control: Use cultivars with resistance genes (R genes)
chemical_control: Limited effectiveness of insecticides for controlling aphids to reduce virus spread

notes: SMV interactions with R genes are studied as a model for gene-for-gene resistance
RNA silencing plays a role in seed transmission and seed coat mottling
Transmission by aphids is influenced by virus proteins HC-Pro and coat protein (CP)
